style_lesson_for_pps_toolkit: Frame the paper around a usable tool, graphical or scriptable workflow, timing-sensitive task support, open materials, and practical examples rather than a new behavioral effect
Explain how studies can be deployed, shared, archived, reused, and adapted while preserving data/security boundaries

brm_examples: vexptoolbox; OpenMaze; The Open Toolbox for Behavioral Research
style_lesson_for_pps_toolkit: Make the design objectives explicit, walk readers through a concrete example, name supported hardware/configuration boundaries, and provide standardized outputs

brm_examples: Timing mega-study; browser psychophysics comparison; jsPsych simulation paper
style_lesson_for_pps_toolkit: Separate usability from timing evidence, encourage local validation on the actual route, and use simulated or automated checks to detect experiment-design errors before interpreting participant data

brm_examples: Auditory synchronization; web timing best practices; web psychoacoustics; headphone screening; touchscreen/keyboard timing; browser/mobile tactile delivery
style_lesson_for_pps_toolkit: Name the participant/device screening procedure, validate the actual sensory route, and keep software logs, physical output, and perceptual evidence as separate claims
